title: [Outdated] Steam Achievements in RPG Maker MZ (using NekoGakuen SteamworksAPI)

posts.author: LaCipolla
posts.body:
This tutorial is outdated as it refers to a guide (and a plugin version) that's not longer online. It will NOT work! See also the replies.
Tutorial topic:
How to integrate steam achievements (and other steam functions) into your RPG Maker MZ game
Brief description:
NekoGakuen Steamworks API is a free plugin for steam integration. It comes with a helpful auto-translated guide ... that leaves quite some room for error. This step-by-step guide builds upon it by explaining some of the more arcane parts and helps with troubleshooting. It's intended for beginners! For the sake of focus, it only deals with Windows and the RMMZ (RPG Maker MZ), even though NekoGakuen can do more than that.
Requirements:
a finished steam page for your game and a working build (
This guide
explains the process!)
a program to zip and unzip files (for example
7-zip
)
an image editing program for the achievement symbols (for example
GIMP
)
NekoGakuen SteamworksAPI
and a few accompanying downloads that will be detailed later
A request before we start:
I'm not a specialist for all of this, but if you have ANY problems with this guide, please leave a comment so I can edit it accordingly! It's only here because I was frustrated with this process myself, so I want to be as clear as humanly possible.
Let's go!
_______
Step 0: Understanding NekoGakuen' files and guide
Perhaps prepare
a handy folder
for all the files we will have in a moment.
Download
the plugin package from itch
.
It's pay what you want, so you can click on "No thanks, just take me to the downloads" for now. If you can afford to get some money to NekoGakuen, you absolutely should! But perhaps wait until we get the plugin to work.
Unzip
the download. Open the "Manual" folder.
In this folder, you'll find
several guides
. Two are in Chinese, but two are English. We need the one for "NWjs".
It's this one:
Alternatively, you could also simply use
this link
.
In the guide, if you click on "Windows" on the left, you will see all the steps of this process.
Look out!
Weirdly, achievements on steam can only be tested once they are already online – which means everybody else can unlock them as well.
One solution to this problem is to create a
playtest version
of your game. My guide won't go into details, but the
steam documentation
helps. Here are some useful things to know:
It's free to create a playtest.
In most aspects, a playtest is a second version of your game, only it doesn't simply show up in the store and can't be played by just anybody (unless you want it to).
While going through the process of creating a playtest, it seems like a big thing, and that's because it can be! But it
doesn't have to be
. If you don't allow people into your playtest, it's only for you!
A playtest has its own app ID, apart from the app ID of your game. Don't mix them up!
It can take Steam some days to unlock your playtest.
For ease of use and to avoid mix-ups, make sure you name your playtest something including "Playtest".
From here on,
the headlines will exactly follow NekoGakuen's steps
, but I will add clarifications and additions where they might be helpful.
Step 1: Download and Install the NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI.js Plugin
We already have the files.
Follow the guide accordingly.
Look out!
The guide gives directions for
RMMV as well as RMMZ
. Don't mix them up!
Look out!
Usually, the
pictures in the guide are very clear
. If you are not sure about some options or files, just focus on the ones that are marked red in these pictures!
The
plugin
can be found under [...\NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI\plugins] and is named "NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI".
It's this one:
Before you continue, you need to
set up your achievements on steam
's app admin page.
It's here.
The guide assumes you already did this.
For each achievement, you need two pictures, usually one in color and one without. To turn a color picture into a grey one, I use the following settings in GIMP: Chroma -100, Lightness -50. The pictures need to be square, with an optimum resolution of 256x256 and a minimum of 64x64.
A simple achievement on steam could look something like this:
For simple achievements, you can ignore the progress stats.
Look out!
What NekoGakuen calls "
Achievement ID
" everywhere is actually called "
API Name
" on steam. This can be confusing, especially when researching online, since steam achievements also had a number called "ID" in the past.
Look out!
In the plugin settings, there is
a function called "Enable Steam Purchase" (Check BuyGame Boolean)
. It tests if you actually bought your game. If your game opens and closes all the time while testing achievements, setting this function to "Disable" can be a useful step.
Step 2: Using the Plugin Command in the Game Project
NekoGakuen has
a lot of functions
. Make sure to take a look at the help text of the plugin. A lot is explained in there!
It might also be a good idea to
start with an easily approachable test event
before implementing all of your achievements!
It could look something like this:
You don't need a
common event
for a simple achievement. It's just an option in case something is supposed to happen after the player unlocks the achievement. If you only want the achievement, set the number to 0.
Step 3: Deploy You Game
I don't have a lot to add here.
Look out!
Some people have
reported problems with project files connected to a cloud service
(like dropbox). There have even been cases with corrupted projects! So if you want to be on the safe side, don't save your working data in your dropbox folder.
Step 4: Download Steamworks SDK
Step 5: Download greenworks.js
Step 6: Download Node Binary Files
Step 7: Download NWjs
Let's do these steps together, because their interaction might
THE biggest pitfall of the whole process
!
Unfortunately it's also the point where NekoGakuen's guide can get a bit confusing (including some inconsistencies), so be ready to reread theirs as well as mine, and perhaps do some troubleshooting!
You don't need to understand all of
these files
(I certainly don't!), but essentially they are updated constantly and
they need to fit together
. There are different "sets" of fitting versions, and the question of how recent the versions are should be secondary to them working together at all!
One set that should work together
well is detailed here:
Steamworks SDK:
download
v1.50
from
this link
greenworks.js:
download the
recent version
from
this link
(the specific version doesn't seem to matter too much here)
Node Binary Files:
download version
v83 (win64)
from
this link
(see below!)
NW.js:
download
v0.49.1 (win64)
from
this link
(
not
the SDK build!)
(If you have other sets that work with NekoGakuen, please comment!)
On how to
find a specific version of the Node Binary Files
on the website: Set the categories on the left as in the following picture. If that doesn't work, just play around a bit until your version (for example v83) pops up.
You don't need a github account
anymore, contrary to what NekoGakuen says.
Step 8: Configure NWjs
To clarify: In this step you take all of your
deployed game files
and copy them into the
unzipped NW.js
(for example v0.49.1).
Be sure to
understand the pictures
from the guide for the correct directions and follow them closely!
I always
rename the nw.exe into Game.exe
(as explained in the guide as "non-essential"), just for clarity.
Step 9: Configure Steamworks SDK
In this step as well, just be sure to
understand the pictures
from the guide for the correct directions and follow them closely!
Look out!
In the guide's pictures you can see that NekoGakuen's Node Binary Files
have another name
("greenworks-win64.node"), and there might be problems if they don't. Just to make sure, rename them.
For example: "
greenworks-nw.js-v83-win32-x64
" -> "
greenworks-win64.node
"
For the app ID, make sure
not to mix up the IDs of your game and your playtest
(in case you are using one).
You can find the IDs in the steam app admin panel. It's here:
And yes, for RMMZ, in the
package.json
, you only need to change one thing: "
rmmz-game
" -> "
GameTitleMZ
"
For a
comparison at this point
, your game folder should look something like this:
And the lib folder:
Now you need to
zip and upload your game to steam
.
Steam has a
direct upload function for smaller games
that works well with the rpg maker and this plugin.
It's here:
Look out!
When
zipping
the files for this function, make sure
the files are NOT placed in another folder
! Inside the zip, you should see the files right away, including the Game.exe etc.
Step 10: Configure Steamworks SDK
Nothing to add here.
In the end,
test if your achievements work and go through the guides again if they don't
!
We are done!

Hi! I'm new to Steamworks and API stuff and I met some problems when I tried to test my game after following the steps here. Guess I need some help!
Edit: I just figure the first one out by disabling "Check BuyGame Boolean".
I'm leaving the rest content here as tips to help if anyone else encounter the same situation (another problem is down below):
When I met the issue, here's what I've already done:
Successfully uploaded my game that WITHOUT NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI.js and the edits mentioned here to Steam
as downloadable live build.
This version ran well but no Steam achievements can be activated of course. (The store page is not yet published, but since the game could be executed I presume it doesn't matter.)
Set up some achievements for testing on Steamwork
, which can be seen on the game page in my library now.
Added a few things in the first event in my game
in order to test the activation and clearance of Steam achievements, and the connection to Steam. (Like "Show Choice" with "Try activate it!" and "Try clear it!" then jump back to the first command.)
Named this edition "API-test version"
.
Prepared the "API-test version"of my game following this guide
, checked that the game folder looks 100% like that is showed here.
Upload "API-test version" via
SteamPipe GUI tool
AND
direct uploading zip file page
, creating 2 builds.
Set these builds to live build of
Default Branch
in turns
, to check if any of them work out.
Publish all the changes
that may cause problem when running the game.
Then I faced a problem and didn't know why or how to fix it:
I could download the game, but FAILED to start it whenever I:
launching it via Steam
clicking the game icon created on my desktop
directly clicking the Game.exe in the folder.
The game window pops up, but before showing anything it shuts down immediately.
When trying with Steam, it would repeating "launches it", "window pops and shut down", "launches it again".
What else I've tried after meeting the problem:
Reset
the version WITHOUT configuring anything following the guide
as live build in Default Branch again, download and launch it.
It runs well like before.
Uninstall the "API-test version", log out Steam and retry
. Nothing changes.
By now I've tried some dozens of times to fix it, and eventually found the solution.
Then another problem comes by:
Does this mean I can only try to activate the achievements or the "Check BuyGame Boolean" after the game officially launched (which means customers can buy & download) on Steam?
Since during playtest with the methods I tried, the achievements aren't activated. And I'm a bit confused about "a finished steam page for your game" in the guide requirement,
does it mean "I have to publish my store page to customers, but the downloadable package can be still pending while I'm editing and testing" or "I can only edit & test it via playtest, with some builds (or achievements themselves) released to the public"?
Hopefully I'm misunderstanding something, cuz once the game is officially published I got no time to adjust anything before players could activate an achievement, and it isn't fair for those who already finished a lot before there are some achievements in the previous process.

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
You can make all the achievement hidden if you don't want the others to look at them before you release the game.
I don't see it in the document,  can a playtest app access the achievements of the main app? I haven't tried that, but you can also create a depot for developer only and add it to developer comp package.
By the way, I don't know if it is also like that in MZ. But I posted in another topic about MV, if you launch the game in your editor using the playtest button, greenworks will think you are playing RMMV, so you won't get achievements for your game that way.

posts.author: LaCipolla
posts.body:
@utunnels
A playtest app cannot access the achievements of the main game, it's really a separate thing. (So the playtest app on steam needs it's own achievement settings.) It could be that you can copy the setting though, I'm not sure right now.
@LunarHillz
I have to admit, I don't understand the
first problem
, so thanks for leaving it here, in case somebody else needs to figure it out! xD' Noob question just for my understanding: "Check BuyGame Boolean" -> How does this work? (Where do I have to go? ^^)

I'm quite sure you do have to publish your game! BUT this is also the purpose of the playtest version: This one you can publish without anybody being able to play (given the correct settings), without publishing your "normal" game first. And it should be able to activate achievements.
Am I missing something?

posts.author: LunarHillz
posts.body:
@LaCipolla
Thanks for explaining!
Glad to hear that I can release the main game & the achievements together!
The first problem
actually occurred to someone else. I saw their comment in the plugin's itch page describing the same situation ("...set up the game on Steam and now when i try to launch it just repeatedly opens and closes the game") and NekoGakuen told them to "try disabling "Check BuyGame Boolean" in the Plugin Manager's Plugins parameter", so I gave it a try and it worked on me!
According to my understanding, the "Check BuyGame Boolean" is for verifying if the player bought this game (or maybe DLCs?) from Steam
, so once I set it true it just went messed up with some Steam functions cuz I technically didn't BUY my test build from Steam. That's how this problem got fixed. And I guess if I want the function of checking players' purchases later, I need to test it with the playtest APP too.
I believe some trouble caused is because it's the first time for developers like me to upload the game to Steam, who may not be sure about how builds, branches, and publishing work exactly so they'd try their best to avoid "accidentally presenting a game package with bugs or unfinished parts to Valve or the public". Doing all the tests locally (stay away from anything related to "publish") sounds safe enough, but unfortunately, the functions just might not work.
Some Addition to the Guide or sth:
Now I have to wait till Valve reviews my store page and playtest page. And today I found
another issue
with my game, that the
NW.js version in the guide seems a bit old
so it causes
text glitches like this
again. I plan to try Greenworks v0.17.0 with NW.js v0.89.0 & Steamworks SDK 1.60, but I actually dunno how to make sure files in steps 4-7 work together. (I dunno how to find the suitable version of the Node Binary File, but Greenworks has one in the zip, I'd try it first)Hope everything goes fine!

its itch page

users' feedback is still gathered around API.js's itch page

NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI.js

NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI.js.

NekoGakuen_SteamworksPlus.js's page

text glitches

I wonder if people still need these files to configure API.js or build something else, they could only test a bunch of versions by themselves to find out which set of them fits or they could usually find the info about required versions in the plugin description or somewhere?

posts.author: LunarHillz
posts.body:
Thanks. My playtest was published yesterday and I just tested a little bit with
NekoGakuen_SteamworksPlus.js
, and the conclusion is
it didn't work
Here's what I did:
Set up achievements for playtest version on Steamworks.
Download the newest version of
NekoGakuen_SteamworksPlus.js
here
and replace
NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI.js
in my project. (NekoGakuen said they've only created a Traditional Chinese version right now, since I can read Traditional Chinese I used this one.)
Set up the parameters and create a test event in my game.
Found that the zip didn't contain folders that were mentioned in "Deploy your game with NWjs" manual
So I turned to try the Electron-based method, prepared the folder as the manual said.
Upload my game to Steam with SteampipeGUI.
Download it from my library and test it.
What I get:
The first build with an added "Choose to unlock/clear the achievement" command
failed to unlock the achievement
.
The second build with two more options: "Choose to unlock/clear the achievement" and then "synchronize the data to the server".
It even failed to be opened
! Gave me
"Failed to load shared library: Cannot find module".
When running the game, all these builds
have the default Electron.exe icon instead of the icon I put in the /icon/ folder on the taskbar
, which never happened when I deploy with NWjs and I dunno how to change it to the right icon I want QwQ
The reasons that may lead to this situation (guessing):
My store page is not published
, so even if everything else around the playtest says "It IS published!" doesn't count. I still need a published store page.
(Edit: It is not necessary to have a published store page since I successfully unlocked the achievement using another method, but I'm not sure if
NekoGakuen's plugins require this.
)
The plugin is still under development,
there are a lot of unknown changes that could cause unexpected bugs
.
I did something wrong
but I cannot tell where did I do wrong.
I'm pretty exhausted now...
I'm even not sure if I should continue drawing achievement icons right now. Maybe later I'll try the
NekoGakuen_SteamworksAPI.js
again to find if any of them works.
Edit: I just found
a simpler way
to activate achievements, but I can't offer any help to other functions that NekoGakuen's plugins can or will do. If you are not in a hurry, you can wait for their improved plugin to be released!
